title: Deadline-aware probe & scheduler exploration
content:
Purpose:

This is a working log for a different angle on continuous-batching scheduler tuning: instead of only tuning batch sizes and timeouts, we explore a lightweight "deadline-aware" probing mechanism that assigns per-request soft deadlines and lets the scheduler opportunistically complete earlier or force smaller micro-batches when tail latency risk is high. Goal: reduce 95th/99th token latency regressions without hurting median throughput more than ~5%.

Why this is different (notes to self):
- Existing experiments cover global timeout/batch-size sweeps; fewer experiments attempted per-request deadlines derived from request-level SLAs and historical service-time samplers.
- Hypothesis: short bursts of long requests (cold KV cache, long context) inflate tail latency; deadline-aware admissions can preemptively adjust fairness weights to protect in-flight low-deadline requests.
- Minimal runtime change: add a cheap pre-scheduler probe that samples expected next-token cost (using history + small micro-inference profiler) and annotates request with deadline quantile.

High-level approach / instrumentation plan:
1) Workloads:
   - Production trace replay (slice: chatbot 1-week sample, 10k reqs/s scaled to test cluster)
   - Synthetic adversarial: mix of short (8 tokens) and long (1024 tokens) sequences, with bursts (10x arrival for 200ms)
   - Stability run: 12h continuous at 80% capacity

2) Scheduler variants to compare (impl flags):
   A. baseline: fixed max-batch=64, timeout=8ms, fairness=round-robin per-route
   B. timeout-tuned: global batch-timeout swept (4/8/12ms) + dynamic batch cap
   C. deadline-probe: each request gets deadline quantile (p50/p90/p99) via a 0.2ms sampler; scheduler prioritizes lower-deadline requests and preempts batch formation if high-risk present
   D. deadline-preemptive: like C but allows breaking forming batch early to schedule an imminent-deadline request (repack into new micro-batch)

3) Metrics (define precisely):
   - latency(token): p50/p90/p95/p99 for next-token generation (not whole response)
   - latency(request): total response end-to-end
   - throughput: tokens/sec across GPU pool
   - utilization: GPU % (smoothed 1s/30s)
   - fairness index: max( per-route p95 ) / median(per-route p95)
   - cost proxy: tokens-per-Joule (measured via cluster power API)

4) Profiling / traces:
   - NVTX ranges around scheduler decisions, batching boundaries, and kernel launches
   - flamegraphs for CPU scheduler threads and per-GPU host threads
   - CUDA kernel breakdown: matmul, softmax, attention, quant-deq, kv cache lookup
   - Host-side: serialization, protobuf parsing, admission logic time

Experiment runs and quick findings (summary for logs below):
- Short runs (30m) at 80% peak showed variant C reduced p99 token latency by ~22% compared to baseline with median throughput drop ~3%.
- Variant D (preemptive) further reduced tail but introduced CPU thrash: host-thread context switches increased ~2.6x and average batch sizes decreased by 9% causing throughput loss ~8% under adversarial bursts.
- The sampler adds median request CPU ~0.18ms; acceptable tradeoff if used adaptively (enable on detected burst windows).

Raw notes / probes (chronological):
2025-09-15 10:12 — initial micro-probe: cheap estimator that replays last 5 token service times for same model, weighted average = expected per-token cost. Fudge factor for cold kv cache: +25% when no recent hits.
2025-09-15 14:03 — NVTX markers added around 'form_batch' and 'admit_request' in C++ scheduler. Observed that 70% of extra tail time correlates with waiting in form_batch for 12ms+.
2025-09-16 09:45 — synthetic burst run (mixed short+long). Baseline p99_token = 328ms. deadline-probe p99_token = 254ms. CPU load up +6%. GPU occupancy unchanged.
2025-09-16 13:20 — deeper flamegraph: host scheduler thread stack top: 'std::mutex::lock' and 'conditionally_wait' while building batches. Preemptive variant forced more wakeups (explain throughput drop).
2025-09-17 11:10 — kernel breakdown on long requests: matmul (60%), kv-cache memcpy (22%), softmax (8%), others 10%. For short requests, kernel overhead dominated by setup (cudaMemcpyAsync) and kernel launch overhead (~1.8ms/call).

Tune ideas and micro-optimizations: (todo list)
- Probe sampling frequency: only sample first request of a user session or every N requests from same connection to reduce overhead.
- Adaptive enabling: use short-term moving average of wait-time-in-queue; enable deadline-probe only when queue wait > p75 baseline.
- Combine with small local micro-batcher: if many low-deadline requests arrive, bundle them into a micro-batch capped at small s (e.g., 8) to keep kernel efficiency.
- Reduce host thrash in preemptive mode: do not preempt a batch if GPU already launched kernels (detect via NVTX or semaphore) — only allow preemption during batch formation window.
- Optimize sampler estimator: use a tiny learned table (per-route lightweight regression) instead of replaying history per-request.

Detailed numbers (from 30-min canonical run, test-cluster-a, baseline vs C vs D):
- Baseline: median_token=12ms, p95=96ms, p99=328ms, throughput=152k tokens/s
- C (deadline-probe): median_token=13ms, p95=86ms, p99=257ms, throughput=147k tokens/s
- D (preemptive): median_token=14ms, p95=78ms, p99=215ms, throughput=140k tokens/s
Notes: throughput measured on same number of GPUs; variance across runs ~2–4% for median; p99 varied more. Energy/cost proxy roughly proportional to throughput * GPU_power; D increased cost per useful token by ~6% vs baseline.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Does probe accuracy decay with model changes (e.g., different quantization, new attention kernel)? Need cross-model validation.
- Stability: long 12h runs show C is stable; D shows slow drift in batch-size distribution and occasional GPU idle spikes after 8h — track mem fragmentation?
- Fairness: investigate per-route throttles combining deadline score and historical watermarks to avoid starving low-throughput routes.

Action items (owners assigned):
- Asha: add adaptive enable heuristic + rollout flag (feature flag). Prepare 24h stability run next week. (PR draft GH#1428)
- Liam: profile sampler's memory footprint and convert to lock-free read path. Look at replacing history replay with lightweight estimator table.
- María: run cross-model validation (7B/13B quantized) and report degradation if any.
- Noah: collect detailed NVTX-correlated traces for 12h run; push to perf-bucket for visualization.

Slack/links (notes):
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime: "deadline-probe initial numbers" (see link pinned in GH issue)
- Related PRs: GH#1410 (batching refactor), GH#1423 (nvtx tracing)

Quick conclusions for PM/leadership one-liner: "A small, adaptive deadline-aware probing mechanism can reduce token-level p99 by ~20–35% in bursty workloads with a modest median throughput tradeoff; aggressive preemption gives more tail benefit but needs host-scheduler optimizations to avoid throughput regressions."

Misc scratch (leave):
- TODO: try combining deadline-probe with kv-cache affinity (if request likely to hit cache, deprioritize? or reverse?)
- TODO: consider model-compiled hints (e.g., model reports expected tokens-per-kernel) to seed estimator

End of doc.
